holidays.name: World Book Night / World Book and Copyright Day
holidays.description: A global celebration of reading, publishing, and authors, where book lovers swap, gift, and snuggle up with their favorite stories. In Catalonia, it doubles as a romantic holiday where people exchange books and roses.
holidays.origin: UNESCO declared April 23 World Book and Copyright Day in 1995, chosen because Shakespeare, Cervantes, and Inca Garcilaso de la Vega all died on this date in 1616 (though under different calendars). The Catalan tradition of Sant Jordi dates back centuries.
holidays.funFact: In Barcelona, roughly 6 million roses and 1.5 million books are sold on this single day, making it one of the biggest book-buying days of the year.

holidays.name: Talk Like Shakespeare Day
holidays.description: A day to hurl Elizabethan insults and wax poetic with thees, thous, and 'forsooth!' Embrace the Bard by greeting coworkers with 'Good morrow, thou artful dodger!'
holidays.origin: An unofficial holiday inspired by Shakespeare's traditional birthday on April 23, 1564, a date that is celebrated although his exact birth date is unknown.
holidays.funFact: Shakespeare is credited with inventing or popularizing hundreds of words and phrases, including 'bedazzled,' 'lonely,' and 'break the ice.'

holidays.name: National Cherry Cheesecake Day
holidays.description: A day for indulging in creamy cheesecake topped with glossy, sweet cherries. Bakers and dessert lovers unite to slice up this tangy, rich treat.
holidays.origin: A food-industry-style observance that grew through dessert enthusiasts and social media, celebrating one of the most popular cheesecake flavors.
holidays.funFact: Cheesecake dates back to ancient Greece, where it was reportedly served to athletes at the first Olympic Games in 776 BC.

holidays.name: Lover's Day (Dia dos Namorados Alt.) / Take a Chance Day
holidays.description: A day encouraging people to step out of their comfort zones, whether by trying a new food, asking someone out, or taking a leap on a wild idea.
holidays.origin: An informal observance popularized in calendars of quirky holidays, meant to remind people that fortune favors the bold.
holidays.funFact: Studies on regret suggest people often regret the chances they didn't take more than the ones they did, which is the whole spirit of this day.

holidays.name: English Language Day (UN)
holidays.description: The United Nations celebrates the English language on this day, honoring its multilingual diversity and rich history, from Old English to modern memes.
holidays.origin: Established by the UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization in 2010 to promote multilingualism and cultural diversity, with the date chosen to coincide with Shakespeare's traditional birthday.
holidays.funFact: English has borrowed words from over 350 other languages, which makes it famously described as a language that follows other languages down dark alleys to rifle through their pockets.
